label: Solution Method
subgoals: Move h(y) under dy and g(x) with dx
Integrate each side in its own variable

slice.rule: An equation is separable when it can be written $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = g(x)\,h(y)$. Divide by $h(y)$, multiply by $dx$, and integrate: $\int \dfrac{dy}{h(y)} = \int g(x)\,dx + C$.
slice.note: Check for constant solutions where $h(y) = 0$; dividing by $h(y)$ loses them.

slice.rule: After integrating, solve for $y$ if you can, absorbing constants: $e^{C}$ becomes a new constant $A$.

label: Initial value version
subgoals: Pick the branch that contains it

slice.rule: Substitute $y(x_0) = y_0$ into the general solution to fix the constant; if solving for $y$ needed a square root or sign choice, take the branch through the initial point.
